input.command: lit comment add hands-architecture-3qr.i3v "Measured on Claude Code 2.1.270: the permission dialog shows at once and the PermissionRequest hook runs beside it; the first answer wins. A keyboard answer does NOT end the hook (it ran to its own 40 s end, output ignored), and nothing in the transcript marks the answer, so the daemon withdraws a waiting reply on the next UserPromptSubmit/Stop/SessionEnd/PermissionRequest and speaks the expiry as what hands did. Reply shape: stdout {hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:PermissionRequest,decision:{behavior:allow}|{behavior:deny,message}}}; empty output decides nothing. Default command hook timeout is 600 s; hands declares 90 s in hookconfig and denies at 85 s. Live run (commit b81630d): voice-path allow -> 'Allowed by PermissionRequest hook', file created; deny -> agent read the message as the tool error and followed it; unanswered -> one warning at 9 s left, deny at 85 s, agent reported it and did not retry. Qwen3-30B on inferno turned 'Yes, go ahead' / 'No, tell it to use git clean instead' into answer_permission allow / deny with that message and the right request id." && lit comment add hands-keyboard-gxr.j7e "From hands-architecture-3qr.i3v: the blocking reply path exists. Sessions.ask holds the hook's connection until a Reply effect; hook_output in src/hands/sessions/hooks.py prints hookSpecificOutput.decision, and core/permissions.py answer() is the pure decider. An AskUserQuestion answer would be Allow with updatedInput, so Allow needs that field and Blocked.on needs the Question variant; the dialog races the hook, so a keyboard answer is only seen as the session moving on."
